A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InfMasking and contain complete, readable main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original InfMasking experiments on Trifeature and real-world multimodal benchmarks, alongside ablations and embedding analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes, including Tables 1–5 and 7–8 and Figures 2–3. Retained results qualify independently of whether experiments were rerun.

M1.justification: Equations (4)–(7) replace masked-to-negative similarity with unmasked-to-negative similarity in the masking loss denominator. Algorithm 1, lines 17–18, makes the corresponding change for both augmentation branches. This revises the specified loss while retaining the architecture, masking procedure, and other objectives; an implementation change or rerun is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Trifeature tasks, MIMIC, MOSI, UR-FUNNY, MUSTARD, Vision&Touch tasks, and MM-IMDb, with the same two- and three-modality coverage. Appendices B and D add no coverage relative to v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within Tables 1–4 and 7: Cross, Cross+Self, FactorCL, MAE, CoMM, CMC, and the relevant SimCLR, CLIP, and SLIP variants are retained in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The linear-probing protocols, dataset splits, metrics, modality configurations, validation-based checkpoint selection, and training budgets are unchanged. Appendix A retains 100 training epochs except 70 for MM-IMDb, and Table 6 retains all experimental configurations.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the same loss-component, masked-view-count, and masking-ratio studies. Appendix D.2's augmentation ablation and Appendix E's Gaussian-assumption visualization are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs with seeds 42–46 and report means and standard deviations in Appendix A and checklist item 7. Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported scores, plotted results, and empirical findings are retained. Examples include 77.0 ± 4.22 synergy accuracy in Table 1 and MM-IMDb weighted/macro F1 scores of 62.60 ± 0.26 and 55.93 ± 0.19 in Table 4. No separate results are reported for the revised loss expression.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects I(X1,X2;Y)=R−S to I(X1;X2;Y)=R−S, distinguishing interaction information from joint mutual information. Lemma 3 and Appendix G revise the negative terms throughout the Jensen/Gaussian derivation. Equation (7) also corrects the covariance quadratic's final factor from z to z'. The assumptions and lemma inventory remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: infinite masking to enhance synergistic information, an efficient loss approximation, and claimed state-of-the-art performance across seven benchmarks. Claim scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The masking mechanism explanation, Gaussian rationale, experimental interpretations, and applicability discussion are unchanged. Both retain limitations concerning the absence of a rigorous synergy framework and increased memory requirements in Section 7 and Appendix C.

D1.justification: Appendix F revises the explicit negative-score calculations in Algorithm 1, lines 17–18, updating the reproducibility pseudocode alongside the loss equations. Hyperparameters, fusion configuration, hardware, data-processing descriptions, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning relative to CoMM, FactorCL, and MAE remains the same, including Appendix D.1.

P1.justification: v3 expands institutional affiliations, adds a laboratory affiliation, and revises the funding acknowledgment. The scientific prose, section ordering, and appendix organization otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter moves the introduction's opening from page 1 to page 2 and reflows text onto page 3. Revised equations and acknowledgments also undergo local reflow. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–8 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the contradictory PID identity and removes mask-dependent negative terms from the claimed Gaussian bound. However, it achieves the latter by changing negative-pair scoring while retaining Section 3.1's InfoNCE definition and every experimental result. The PDFs neither reconcile these estimator definitions nor establish whether the edits correct the description of the evaluated method or change that method. These benefits and unresolved consistency issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
